embedded_tokens: [0] meta[http-equiv=refresh] on Cloudflare challenge page — numeric refresh interval 360 seconds, not a CSRF but indicates timed challenge refresh.

[1] meta[name=robots] on home page — value 'index,follow' (SEO directive, no secret), plus two meta[name=google-site-verification] tokens with long opaque strings used for Google Search Console site ownership verification.
[2] meta[name=robots] on SUVs SRP — value 'index, follow' (SEO directive, not secret).
[3] meta[name=robots] on VDP — value 'index,follow' (SEO directive, not secret).
[4] meta[name=robots] on cars SRP — value 'index, follow' (SEO directive, not secret).

[1] __NEXT_DATA__ script tag on home page — large JSON blob (~445 KB) containing clientId, correlationId, browserCookieId, experiments, internal link groups, and various context objects, including opaque IDs and cookie values but no obvious public API keys.

[2] App Router flight data scripts on SUVs SRP (multiple self.__next_f pushes) — streamed React/Next flight data containing route tree, cookie names/values (e.g., CVCurrentCity, BrowserCookieId, mdt-session-id), experiment buckets, and configuration flags; treated as server-rendered data rather than classical CSRF tokens.

[2] application/ld+json[data-qa=vehicle-ld] scripts on SUVs SRP — repeated Vehicle schema objects including VINs, SKU numbers, and price data for many vehicles; sensitive identifiers but standard structured data, not auth tokens.

[3] __NEXT_DATA__ script tag on VDP — JSON (~41 KB) with clientId 'vdp_ui', correlationId, browserCookieId, searchRequestId, vehicleId, configuration flags, and serverCookies snapshot (e.g., __cf_bm, BrowserCookieId) but no recognizable API key.

[4] App Router flight data scripts on cars SRP (self.__next_f) — similar to SUVs SRP: cookies (CVCurrentCity/State/Zip, BrowserCookieId), experiment cookies, configuration and SEO link data; again opaque IDs but no explicit CSRF/meta auth tokens.

[1,2,3,4] Various analytics/ads scripts (GTM, gtag, Facebook Pixel, Bing, Snowplow, Spotify pixel, ImpactRadius) include IDs like GTM-PCCP2G, G-YGPT2P3T9Z, AW-928301978, Facebook pixel ID 2178741032440639, Snowplow appId 'carvana-3cb788c9-22ed-412c-b607-d16c9a38cc81' — these are tracking identifiers, not user-specific tokens.
data_blobs: [0] Cloudflare inline challenge script on 'Just a moment...' page — window._cf_chl_opt object with cZone, cRay, cH, UTM-like tokens and encoded parameters (~5.5 KB), used by Cloudflare Turnstile to orchestrate the bot challenge.

[1] script#__NEXT_DATA__ on home page — massive Next.js data blob (~445 KB) containing props.pageProps for 'home_ui' including deviceTypeProps, experimentContext (experiment names and buckets), internalLinksGroups (body styles, top locations), and various configuration flags (gtmId, feature toggles).

[2] Numerous application/ld+json[data-qa=vehicle-ld] scripts on SUVs SRP — each is a Vehicle schema JSON with fields like name, modelDate, manufacturer, VIN, mileageFromOdometer, price, priceCurrency, availability, and canonical VDP URL; about two dozen such blobs describing search results.

[2] React/Next App Router flight data scripts (self.__next_s and many self.__next_f pushes) on SUVs SRP — serialized React tree and router state including route structure, stylesheets, cookies (BrowserCookieId, CVCurrent*), configuration (useSrpAppRouter, VINWhyBuyNarrativeConfig), and SEO metadata; very large combined payload (>600 KB).

[3] script#__NEXT_DATA__ on VDP — Next.js page data for 'vdp_ui' including acquisition, analytics, and common static context, with payloadMetaAttributes (inventoryType, offering, page, searchRequestId, vehicleId), configuration flags, and serverCookies snapshot; medium-sized JSON (~41 KB).
[3] Single application/ld+json Vehicle schema on VDP head — describes the specific 2025 Chevrolet Trailblazer (VIN, SKU, mileage, price, offers) for rich snippets.

[4] application/ld+json[data-qa=vehicle-ld] scripts on cars SRP — many Vehicle schema blobs similar to SUVs SRP but covering a broader set of vehicles and colors, each with VIN, price, and URL; dozens of such entries.

[4] App Router flight data scripts on cars SRP (self.__next_f) — same pattern as SUVs SRP: route tree, cookies, filters context (none initially), SEO internalLinks (bodyStyles, bodyStylesYears, topLocations), and configuration; large streaming JSON-like payload.
[1,2,3,4] Web-vitals polyfill inline scripts — small inline JS to polyfill first input delay metrics; not data blobs but repeated shared code across pages.
narrative: Navigation sequence: user first hits a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge at https://www.carvana.com/, then is allowed through to the Next.js-powered Carvana home page, navigates to the SUVs search results (App Router /cars/suv), then to a specific VDP (pages router /vehicle/[vehicleId]), and finally to the general used-cars SRP (/cars). All main app pages (home, SRPs, VDP) are clearly built on Next.js/React: the home and VDP use the classic pages router with a single __NEXT_DATA__ JSON blob plus _next/static chunk scripts, while the SRPs use the newer App Router with React Server Components flight data via self.__next_f/self.__next_s and many _next/static/chunks/app/... scripts. The home page exposes one primary search form (search bar with input+button) and the SRPs each expose a simple keyword search input form; no login, checkout, or multi-field forms appear in these snapshots, and there are no CSRF meta tags or hidden inputs. Embedded tokens are mostly SEO/verification (robots, google-site-verification) and analytics IDs (GTM, gtag, FB pixel, Snowplow), with more sensitive but still expected cookie IDs and VINs living inside __NEXT_DATA__, App Router flight data, and ld+json Vehicle blobs. The SRPs and VDP both provide rich structured data via many application/ld+json Vehicle entries, describing inventory in detail (VIN, price, mileage, URLs) for search engines. No HTML <table> elements are present; all lists and grids (vehicle tiles, filters) are rendered as div-based React components. Overall, this is a single-page-like React/Next.js application with heavy client-side chunking, server-rendered JSON configuration, and marketing/analytics integrations, fronted by Cloudflare for bot protection.
